title: Physicochemical fingerprinting reveals convergent evolutionary determinants of enterovirus A71 neurovirulence through integrative machine learning and structural analysis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) causes hand, foot, and mouth disease and can trigger life-threatening neurological complications, yet the sequence-level physicochemical correlates of CNS involvement across globally circulating lineages remain incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here we screened 15,247 EV-A71 genomic entries spanning 1998-2024, retaining 267 full-length sequences (≥7,000 bp) with confirmed clinical outcomes (7 central nervous system [CNS]-involved, 260 non-CNS).
analysis.methods: Each polyprotein position was encoded by three Z-scale descriptors-hydrophobicity (Z1), molecular volume (Z2), and electrostatic polarity (Z3)-converting discrete residue identities into a continuous biophysical feature space. A two-stage statistical pipeline (Mann-Whitney U screening followed by odds-ratio ranking) distilled 20 significant loci down to five core positions. Leave-one-out cross-validated logistic regression achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.889) among eight algorithms benchmarked.
analysis.main_results: SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) assigned the largest model contribution to P2124_Z1 (OR = 4.28; 95% CI 1.47-12.51), while P1246_Z3 was statistically associated with lower CNS odds (OR = 0.50).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Reference-strain mapping linked the five polyprotein coordinates to mature-protein residues in 3D RdRp, 3C protease, 2C helicase, and 2A, thereby providing structural context for cautious biochemical hypotheses rather than confirmed mechanisms. The study presents the five-position physicochemical signature and nomogram as hypothesis-generating tools for prioritising candidate neurovirulence markers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a framework for prioritising candidate neurovirulence markers, which could inform surveillance and early detection of high-risk EV-A71 strains. The identified physicochemical signature may guide future studies on pathogenesis and therapeutic targeting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This extreme 7:260 class imbalance, reflecting the scarcity of publicly available full-length CNS-associated EV-A71 genomes, is the principal limitation and interpretive premise of the study. Because the AUC is estimated from only seven positive samples, it should be regarded as an exploratory internal performance signal rather than definitive evidence of generalisable accuracy, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the physicochemical determinants of EV-A71 neurovirulence by analyzing 267 full-length genomes (7 CNS-involved, 260 non-CNS) from 1998-2024. Using machine learning and structural analysis, researchers identified five key polyprotein positions (P2124_Z1, P997_Z2, P1246_Z3, P1743_Z2, P1711_Z1) significantly associated with CNS involvement. The model achieved an AUC of 0.889, though limited by the small number of CNS genomes. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing neurovirulence markers, requiring validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

title: Efficacy and Mechanisms of Alkaloids Against Enterovirus A71: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Preclinical Evidence Integrated with Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking

analysis.scope_and_question: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease, yet no specific antiviral therapy has been approved.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This study systematically evaluated the efficacy and mechanisms of alkaloids against EV-A71 infection by integrating meta-analysis, network pharmacology, and molecular docking. Nine animal studies were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Meta-analysis suggested that alkaloid intervention significantly improved survival (OR = 30.62, 95% CI: 10.44–89.82), reduced clinical severity, attenuated body weight loss, and decreased viral loads in infected tissues. Network pharmacology predicted 155 shared targets between seven active alkaloids and EV-A71-related genes, with MAPK1, MAPK3, JUN, AURKB, and MAPK8 recognized as core targets. Functional enrichment analysis suggested significant involvement of the MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 signaling pathways. Molecular docking provided computational support for stable binding affinities between active alkaloids and core targets (−6.7 to −9.3 kcal/mol).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analyses preliminarily suggested that quinolizidine alkaloids and high-dose regimens (>5 mg/kg) may be associated with preclinical intervention effects.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings support the potential of alkaloids as candidates for the development of novel anti-EV-A71 therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and mechanisms of alkaloids against Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), a major cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease with no approved specific therapy. Integrating meta-analysis, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, the study included nine animal studies. Results showed alkaloid intervention significantly improved survival (OR = 30.62), reduced clinical severity, attenuated weight loss, and decreased viral loads. Network pharmacology identified 155 shared targets, with MAPK1, MAPK3, JUN, AURKB, and MAPK8 as core targets, and highlighted involvement of MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 pathways. Molecular docking confirmed stable binding affinities (−6.7 to −9.3 kcal/mol). Subgroup analyses suggested quinolizidine alkaloids and high-dose regimens (>5 mg/kg) may be particularly effective. The findings support alkaloids as promising candidates for novel anti-EV-A71 therapeutics through direct antiviral and host-directed mechanisms.

title: A dual-receptor checkpoint primes enterovirus D68 for respiratory cell entry

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the molecular mechanism by which enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) invades respiratory cells, focusing on the newly identified receptor MFSD6 and its role in viral entry.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed near-atomic-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to analyze historical and contemporary AFM-associated EV-D68 strains and their complexes with the third extracellular loop of MFSD6 (MFSD6-L3).
analysis.methods: Structural analyses were conducted to determine the virus-receptor engagement mechanism, followed by functional analyses to define the contributions of receptor-contacting residues and glycans to viral attachment and entry.
analysis.main_results: The study revealed a previously unrecognized 'binary gating switch' mechanism where the N200-V208 segment of MFSD6 inserts into one capsomer, while its sialyl-Gal-terminated glycan engages an adjacent capsomer, with Neu5Ac binding inducing conformational rearrangements that prime infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as refining the molecular basis of EV-D68 recognition of MFSD6 and revealing a glycan-mediated dual-lock mechanism that enhances receptor specificity and ensures productive infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide broader insight into enterovirus tropism and establish a framework for structure-guided antiviral design, potentially informing strategies to prevent EV-D68 infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the use of near-atomic-resolution cryo-EM and functional analyses, though limitations may include the specificity of the findings to EV-D68 and potential generalizability to other enteroviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) uses the respiratory receptor MFSD6 to enter cells, revealing a novel 'binary gating switch' mechanism. Through near-atomic-resolution cryo-electron microscopy, the researchers discovered that EV-D68 engages MFSD6 via two distinct interactions: a protein segment insertion and glycan binding. This dual-receptor checkpoint mechanism primes the virus for infection by inducing conformational changes that destabilize the virion. The findings enhance our understanding of enterovirus tropism and provide a foundation for developing targeted antiviral therapies against EV-D68, a virus causing severe respiratory disease and poliomyelitis-like illness in children.

title: Neurotropism and interferon-dominated immune responses in a mouse-adapted coxsackievirus A16 infection model

analysis.research_question_and_background: The development of animal models infected with Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) is limited by insufficient neurovirulence, which hinders the study of pathogenesis mechanisms and antiviral drug evaluation. The lack of animal models that reliably recapitulate the neurological manifestations of Coxsackievirus A16 infection has constrained progress in understanding CVA16 neuropathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We aimed to develop a neonatal ICR mouse model for CVA16 infection, wherein infected brain tissue was continuously passaged from 2-day-old ICR suckling mice, resulting in a highly neurovirulent mouse-adapted strain (CVA16-P5) to establish optimal infection conditions for antiviral assessment. By systematically optimizing viral dose, inoculation route, and age at infection, we defined conditions that reproducibly induced progressive neurological disease and multisystem involvement.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing identified a nonsynonymous mutation in the VP1 capsid protein associated with enhanced neurovirulence during mouse adaptation. Transcriptomic analysis of neural tissues revealed tissue-specific interferon-dominated immune responses and signatures of systemic viral dissemination that recapitulate key features of severe human infection.
analysis.main_results: Infection with the CVA16-P5 strain resulted in consistent pathological alterations across multiple tissues, accompanied by characteristic neurological manifestations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The CVA16-P5-adapted strain infection model provides a robust experimental platform for investigating CVA16 pathogenesis and for the preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses. This model enables the analysis of tissue-specific immune responses, viral dissemination, and genetic determinants of neurovirulence, including a VP1 mutation associated with enhanced pathogenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: By providing a reproducible and physiologically relevant system for studying severe CVA16 infection, the CVA16-P5-adapted strain infection model setup in this study supports mechanistic studies of CVA16 pathogenesis and facilitates the preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high as the study provides a well-characterized mouse model with reproducible neurological disease and molecular insights into neurovirulence.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a neonatal ICR mouse model for Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) infection by passaging virus in brain tissue to create a highly neurovirulent strain (CVA16-P5). The model reproducibly induces progressive neurological disease and multisystem pathology, with transcriptomic analysis revealing tissue-specific interferon-dominated immune responses and systemic viral dissemination. Whole-genome sequencing identified a VP1 capsid protein mutation associated with enhanced neurovirulence. This robust experimental platform enables mechanistic studies of CVA16 pathogenesis and preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses.

title: Pathogenic Surveillance and Genetic Characteristics of Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease Pathogens in Xi'an, 2020-2024.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common pediatric infectious disease that frequently causes outbreaks in the Asia-Pacific region. The lack of cross-protection among serotypes highlights the need for multivalent vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Epidemiologic data and clinical specimens were collected from reported HFMD cases in Xi'an between 2020 and 2024. Among 2596 specimens, 2148 (82.7%) were enterovirus-positive.
analysis.methods: Pan-enterovirus, enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), and coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) were detected by real-time polymerase chain reaction. The VP1 regions of CVA6 and CVA16 were amplified, sequenced, and phylogenetically analyzed.
analysis.main_results: The proportions of detected viruses were: CVA6 52.8%, CVA16 23.8%, CVA10 5.0%, and EV-A71 0.3%. CVA6 predominated in 2020, 2022, and 2023, while CVA16 predominated in 2021 and 2024. Compared with CVA16 infection, CVA6 infection was associated with younger age (3.25 vs. 4.14 years, P < 0.001) and a higher risk of severe disease (OR = 12.93).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: CVA6 and CVA16 are the predominant HFMD pathogens in Xi'an with alternating circulation. All identified CVA6 strains belonged to the D3a subtype, whereas the B1a subtype predominated among CVA16 strains.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The first emergence of the CVA16 B1c sublineage in 2024 mirrors national trends and warrants intensified surveillance. The findings provide insights into the changing epidemiology of HFMD pathogens, which can inform vaccine development and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on reported HFMD cases and clinical specimens, which may not capture all circulating strains. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data and does not include experimental controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the pathogenic surveillance and genetic characteristics of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) pathogens in Xi'an from 2020 to 2024. It identifies that coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6) and coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) are the predominant pathogens, with alternating circulation over the study period. CVA6 was associated with younger age and a higher risk of severe disease. All CVA6 strains were classified as subgenotype D3a, while CVA16 strains were categorized into B1a, B1b, and B1c subtypes, with B1a being the most prevalent. The emergence of the B1c lineage in 2024 is noted as a significant trend. The study highlights the need for intensified surveillance and the potential for multivalent vaccines due to the lack of cross-protection among serotypes. However, the findings are based on observational data and may not fully account for all circulating strains, limiting the strength of the evidence.

title: Enterovirus Encephalitis Developing After Treatment for Follicular Lymphoma: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report a rare case of chronic enteroviral encephalitis developing in a patient undergoing rituximab maintenance therapy for follicular lymphoma, highlighting the risk of severe enteroviral complications in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with stage IV, grade 3A follicular lymphoma who developed chronic enteroviral encephalitis during rituximab maintenance therapy after achieving complete remission with R-CHOP.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR to confirm enterovirus infection.
analysis.main_results: The patient presented with confusion and involuntary movements shortly after the sixth rituximab maintenance dose, and cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR confirmed enterovirus infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret chronic enteroviral encephalitis as a rare but serious complication in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving B-cell-depleting therapies like rituximab.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings emphasize the need for heightened awareness and monitoring of enteroviral infections in patients on anti-CD20 therapies to prevent severe neurological complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the case report design, which lacks a control group and cannot establish causality, though the diagnostic confirmation provides moderate confidence in the reported association.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with stage IV, grade 3A follicular lymphoma who developed chronic enteroviral encephalitis during rituximab maintenance therapy. After achieving complete remission with six cycles of R-CHOP, she received rituximab every three months and presented with confusion and involuntary movements after the sixth dose. Cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR confirmed enterovirus infection. The authors highlight that chronic enteroviral encephalitis is a rare but serious complication in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving B-cell-depleting therapies. The findings underscore the importance of monitoring for enteroviral infections in such patients to prevent severe neurological outcomes.
